packages.title: UK ETS maritime first half-year QA
facts: The first UK ETS maritime scheme year runs from 1 July to 31 December 2026.
Later maritime scheme years run by calendar year from 1 January to 31 December.
The first maritime period is therefore a six-month compliance period.
A partial scheme year must not be treated as a full-year emissions period.
No parcel value is inferred from scheme timing.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime gas-species scope QA
facts: UK ETS maritime monitoring covers carbon dioxide, nitrous oxide and methane.
The three gases are converted to CO2-equivalent for compliance.
Gas species should remain identifiable before aggregation.
Air pollutants outside the UK ETS maritime GHG scope are not substituted into this total.
No parcel emissions are inferred from vessel reporting rules.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime allowance surrender ratio QA
facts: For each tonne of CO2e in the maritime emissions figure for surrender, one allowance must be surrendered.
The emissions figure for surrender can differ from raw monitored emissions when an applicable surrender deduction is used.
Allowances are compliance instruments rather than physical emissions.
The surrender figure must preserve the scheme-defined calculation.
No land parcel emissions are inferred from allowance surrender.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime reporting and surrender deadlines QA
facts: Maritime annual emissions reports are due by 31 March following the scheme year.
The 2026 and 2027 maritime scheme years use a 30 April 2028 surrender deadline.
From the 2028 scheme year onward, surrender is due by 30 April following the scheme year.
Reporting and surrender are distinct compliance events.
A filing deadline is not evidence of an emissions quantity.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime 42-day monitoring-plan rule QA
facts: A maritime operator may need to apply for an emissions monitoring plan within 42 days of an in-scope maritime activity.
The monitoring plan establishes how emissions will be monitored and calculated.
Plan approval is separate from annual verified emissions reporting.
A monitoring plan is not itself measured emissions.
No parcel value is inferred from plan status.

packages.title: Farm Practices Survey 54 percent GHG importance QA
facts: In the February 2026 Farm Practices Survey, 54% of farms considered GHG emissions fairly or very important to farm decisions.
The result applies to surveyed holdings in England.
The measure is a survey response, not measured emissions.
Survey percentages must preserve their question and denominator.
No farm parcel CO2e is inferred from stated importance.

packages.title: Farm Practices Survey 47 percent action QA
facts: The 2026 survey reports 47% of farmers were actively implementing measures to lower farm GHG emissions.
Action status is self-reported survey information.
Adoption of an action is not equivalent to a quantified emissions reduction.
The statistic applies at England survey level.
No parcel reduction value is inferred.

packages.title: Farm Practices Survey recycling action QA
facts: Among farms taking GHG-reduction action, 75% reported recycling waste materials from the farm.
The percentage is conditional on holdings taking action.
Recycling activity can influence emissions but is not itself a CO2e value.
The denominator must not be changed to all farms without evidence.
No parcel emissions reduction is assigned.

packages.title: Farm Practices Survey energy-efficiency action QA
facts: Among farms taking GHG-reduction action, 69% reported improving energy efficiency.
Energy-efficiency action is distinct from measured energy savings.
Measured energy savings are also distinct from GHG reductions unless compatible factors are applied.
The statistic is a survey adoption rate.
No parcel result is inferred.

packages.title: Farm Practices Survey manure-efficiency action QA
facts: In 2026, 45% of action-taking farms reported improving manure or slurry management and application efficiency.
The survey notes this action has increased substantially since 2013.
Management-practice adoption is not measured nitrous-oxide or methane reduction.
Inventory models require separate activity and emissions-factor evidence.
No parcel reduction is fabricated.

packages.title: Farm Practices Survey methane-suppressing feed QA
facts: The 2026 survey reports 2% of farms regularly fed methane-suppressing feed products to livestock.
The percentage describes adoption, not methane mass avoided.
Livestock type and feeding conditions can affect emissions outcomes.
The result should not be generalized to all holdings without the survey denominator.
No parcel methane reduction is inferred.

packages.title: Agriculture around 13 percent UK GHG QA
facts: Defra reports agriculture accounts for around 13% of UK greenhouse gases.
The figure is a national sector share.
Agriculture emits nitrous oxide, methane and carbon dioxide.
A sector share does not identify emissions of a specific holding.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: Agriculture 59 percent UK nitrous oxide QA
facts: Defra reports agriculture accounted for 59% of UK nitrous oxide emissions in 2024.
Nitrous oxide is a greenhouse gas.
Agricultural soils and nitrogen management are important sources.
The national share is not a farm-specific measurement.
No parcel N2O value is inferred.

packages.title: Agriculture 49 percent UK methane QA
facts: Defra reports agriculture accounted for 49% of UK methane emissions in 2024.
Enteric fermentation is an important agricultural methane source.
Methane is reported separately before CO2e aggregation.
The national percentage is not a holding-level measurement.
No parcel methane value is inferred.

packages.title: Agriculture 2.5 percent UK carbon dioxide QA
facts: Defra reports agriculture accounted for 2.5% of UK carbon dioxide emissions in 2024.
The CO2 share is much smaller than agriculture's methane and nitrous-oxide shares.
Gas-specific shares must not be confused with the overall agriculture GHG share.
The statistic is national in scope.
No parcel CO2 value is inferred.

packages.title: Agriculture 89 percent ammonia non-GHG guard QA
facts: Defra reports agriculture accounted for 89% of UK ammonia emissions in 2024.
Ammonia is an air pollutant rather than a greenhouse gas.
Ammonia can contribute indirectly to nitrous-oxide formation after deposition.
The ammonia percentage must not be inserted directly into GHG totals.
No parcel CO2e is inferred from ammonia share.

packages.title: Agricultural emissions 15 percent long-term fall QA
facts: Defra reports estimated agricultural greenhouse-gas and air-pollution emissions fell 15% between 1990 and 2024.
The statement is a long-term sector trend.
Inventory methods are revised annually as evidence improves.
A national trend does not imply the same change for every farm.
No parcel trend is inferred.

packages.title: 2026 slurry LESSE methodology change QA
facts: Planned 2026 UK GHG inventory changes update slurry-management modelling for low-emission slurry spreading equipment.
The update uses country-specific uptake data for cattle and pig slurry in England.
Different geographic assumptions are used where country-specific data are unavailable.
DESNZ describes the overall emissions impact of this change as negligible.
Methodological change is preserved rather than treated as observed parcel change.

packages.title: 2026 grass yield and nitrogen methodology change QA
facts: Planned inventory changes update grassland assumptions for grass yield and nitrogen uptake.
The change affects estimated nitrous-oxide emissions from grass residues and nitrogen leaching.
Model assumptions can move estimated emissions without a new physical measurement at every location.
Historical series can be revised when the model changes.
No parcel emissions are inferred from a national methodology change.

packages.title: 2026 ammonia indirect N2O methodology QA
facts: A planned method estimates ammonia emissions from decomposition of plant residues on the soil surface.
Ammonia is an air pollutant, not a greenhouse gas.
Deposited ammonia can act as an indirect source of nitrous oxide.
The methodology change can therefore affect GHG inventory estimates indirectly.
Ammonia mass is not directly relabelled as parcel CO2e.

packages.title: 2026 sheep grass-energy methodology change QA
facts: Planned inventory changes update sheep assumptions for grass energy content using survey evidence.
The change increases estimated grass intake needed to meet energy requirements.
Higher estimated intake can increase enteric methane estimates.
Related grass crude-protein assumptions also affect nitrous-oxide estimates over the time series.
The model update is not a direct parcel measurement.
